reason: Generates synthetic defect images with a Siamese validation stage to balance minority classes, but the purpose is semantic segmentation of surface defects rather than classification (clarification 1).
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes Hash-space SMOTE, interpolating with local noise inside LSH buckets, supported only by a complexity analysis.
Proposes a diffusion-based conditional generator that concentrates synthetic samples in under-sampled regions to mitigate data imbalance in tasks such as classification, with extensive experiments.
No abstract, and the title's hybrid class imbalance technique inside an electricity theft stacking model could be a new resampling method or an applied existing one.
Presents SMOTE combined with rough random forest as an extension of SMOTE to big data, but the abstract does not say whether SMOTE's application changes or SMOTE is only a preprocessing step.

The new k-means-centroid sampling is framed as an undersampling improvement and combined with standard SMOTE inside an attack detector, and the abstract does not show whether this changes how synthetic examples are made.
The diabetes readmission study claims a specifically tailored, improved SMOTE but never says what changes, so the abstract cannot tell whether the resampling is the authors' own.
The bearing fault diagnosis pipeline uses a standard WGAN module for augmentation alongside first-order meta-learning for few-shot diagnosis, and no change to the generator is described.
Introduces conformational oversampling, which generates extra conformations of minority molecules to balance imbalanced toxicity data, evaluated on Tox21.

A thesis with a Greek title that builds a comparative framework of random undersampling, SMOTE and single and subtype-specific WGAN-GP oversampling for predictive maintenance without proposing a new method, and as a thesis it also fails I3.
The neonatal framework changes CTGAN generation by relaxing feature bounds and filters synthetic samples by silhouette score, a change to the generation that clarification 3 includes.
I2 not stated in the abstract: Adversarial SMOTE learns interpolation coefficients from classifier feedback in a bi-level loop, but no data or experiments are named.
The fraud detection pipeline augments data with a named S-HeMOTE oversampler, and the abstract does not say whether it is the authors' own variant or an existing one.
Existing SMOTE joined with the existing cross-validated committees noise filter is presented as a SMOTE extension, with no change to the generation described (clarification 3).
RN-SMOTE chains standard SMOTE, DBSCAN removal of noisy synthetic points and a second SMOTE pass, an existing generator plus an existing cleaning step presented as a new method (clarification 3).
I2 not stated in the abstract: after reviewing imbalance techniques it proposes a novel oversampling technique for binary classification but names no evaluation.

The proposed framework generates minority samples with class-specific GANs in an autoencoder latent space, credits latent augmentation for handling imbalance, and is evaluated on AML-Cytomorphology-LMU.
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes a GFlowNet plus VGAE generator of synthetic rare-class drug interaction samples, but offers only a general performance claim with no data or experiments named.
The fraud study calls its mix of synthetic oversampling and undersampling a proposed hybrid resampling method without describing any change to generation (clarification 3).
Presents a new class balancing mechanism based on an interquartile minority oversampling technique as a contribution and evaluates it on SGCC smart meter data.
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes MRC-SMOTE with multi-resolution kernel folding and interpolation, supported only by theoretical analysis.
The proposed resampling pairs an existing WGAN oversampler with random undersampling and describes no change to the generation (clarification 3).
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes DTG-SMOTE, which confines neighbour selection and interpolation to CART leaf paths, supported only by theoretical analysis.
Proposes four domain-knowledge sampling strategies, but the abstract does not say whether any of them generates synthetic examples or changes how SMOTE is applied rather than only undersampling.
The IoT intrusion paper generates minority traffic with a tailored CTGAN but does not say what was changed, so it cannot tell whether the generator is the authors' own.
The sEMG activity recognition framework employs a boundary midpoint centroid SMOTE whose origin the abstract does not give, so it cannot tell whether this variant is the authors' own.

Existing SVM-SMOTE and EasyEnsemble undersampling are combined as data processing before a tuned XGBoost and presented as a new algorithm, with no change to the generation described (clarification 3).

The bearing fault method feeds FFT spectra to a standard GAN to synthesize minority fault samples in a diagnosis pipeline and compares it with ROS and SMOTE, with no change to the generator described.
Beyond the SMOTE-RUS-NC combination, it embeds the sampling inside a balanced random forest (SRN-BRF), changing where synthetic examples are made, and is evaluated on 26 datasets.
Adds caching and minority class oversampling to online learners for imbalanced streams, but the abstract does not say whether synthetic examples are generated or minority examples are only replayed.
Proposes a wrapper that searches the amounts of SMOTE generation and undersampling by f-value, a new way of setting SMOTE's sample allocation, evaluated on several datasets.
An agentic diffusion and LLM generator of synthetic instances for rare classes, built for long-tailed object detection and instance segmentation rather than classification (clarification 1).
Uses SMOTE-NC inside a new method whose purpose is missing-value imputation for imbalanced mixed-type data, not oversampling for classification (clarification 1).
No abstract, and the title names IOSMOTE inside a cross-project defect prediction method, which may be a new or an existing SMOTE variant.
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes Abstraction-level SMOTE, which interpolates in an encoder latent space and decodes back, supported only by theoretical analysis.
The cross-project defect pipeline applies a grouped SMOTE followed by density-based data selection, and the abstract does not say whether grouped SMOTE is the authors' own way of applying SMOTE.

DiffusionAAE generates class-conditional hyperspectral samples mainly to cope with limited labels and high dimensionality, and the abstract does not say it oversamples minority classes (clarification 1).

Studies likelihood-ranked selection of synthetic samples in self-consuming diffusion training, whose purpose is model collapse and minority-mode retention, not imbalanced classification (clarification 1).

Applies existing oversamplers only to the short-ORF coding RNA subgroup to fix local imbalance, and the abstract cannot tell whether this targeting is a resampling method of its own or a domain preprocessing step.
Proposes an extension of the deep over-sampling framework that uses weak abstract labels for many-class imbalanced image classification, with an empirical study on benchmarks.
No abstract; the title announces a deep-learning-based oversampling scheme for imbalanced classification, but its evaluation and the language of a paper in a Korean venue cannot be checked.
Applies a GAN-based oversampler with boosted trees to credit card fraud and compares it with SMOTE, ROS and ADASYN, with no change to the generator described.
The intrusion detection CNN starts with an unspecified oversampling based on deep-learning image processing, and the abstract cannot tell whether that oversampler is new.
The web spam framework preprocesses data with a new Split by Over-sampling and Train by Under-fitting technique, but the abstract does not say whether it generates synthetic examples.
No abstract, and the title's CASE and C-BAFT image processing techniques for multiclass skin disease CNNs may or may not generate synthetic minority images.

Introduces a methodology that integrates hybrid undersampling and oversampling within ensemble classifiers for multiclass intrusion detection, a resampling-inside-ensemble hybrid evaluated on CHADC2020 and IoTID20.
Presents metaheuristic (IMOWPA) selection of SMOTE's number of neighbours as a novel element, a change to neighbour choice, evaluated on MIMIC III.
The hybrid DNN, GAN and feature selection detector does not say whether the GAN generates minority attack samples or whether it is new, and reports no results.
The hyperspectral corn pipeline fuses an ensemble oversampling method with pixel pair augmentation and ensemble training, and the abstract cannot tell whether the oversampling itself is new.
No abstract, but a book chapter with the generic title Handling Imbalanced Data Sets is most likely a tutorial overview rather than a method paper.

The software defect study combines standard SMOTE with bagging and boosting on NASA data, existing resampling and ensembles applied to a domain problem with no change to how SMOTE is applied described.
BSS-ENN pairs existing Borderline-SMOTE with existing ENN cleaning and is benchmarked against other hybrids, an existing generator plus cleaning step presented as new (clarification 3).
OS-YATSI combines semi-supervised learning with an unspecified oversampling strategy for defect severity, and the abstract cannot tell whether the oversampling or its use is new.
Although indexed as a review, the garbled abstract proposes a regression-based approach that creates new pattern samples for imbalanced data, compared with SMOTE in class prediction experiments.
A coupled-GAN feature generator built for zero-shot learning of unseen classes, a purpose other than imbalanced classification (clarification 1).
The bearing fault diagnosis method's novelty is an ABC-optimized OS-ELM, while its resampling uses existing K-means SMOTE with distance-based undersampling.
Anticancer peptide prediction proposes an innovative DC-GAN augmentation for underrepresented peptide types, but the abstract does not say whether the DC-GAN is changed or applied as is.
The brain tumour segmentation model incorporates an undescribed modified SMOTE in preprocessing, so the abstract cannot tell whether the change is the authors' own, and the task is segmentation.
The new three-step oversampling serves transformer remaining-useful-life prediction with AdaBoost regression, a regression task with no classification.
The fraud architecture uses an off-the-shelf CTGAN to generate minority samples for a BERT classifier, and no change to the generator is described.
Bal-IDS designs a balancing method whose first stage is an adaptive oversampling strategy, and the abstract cannot tell whether that oversampling is new or generates synthetic samples.
Proposes a hybrid mixup strategy tailored to long-tailed imbalance that synthesizes mixed training examples, with a two-head network, evaluated on long-tail recognition benchmarks.
Develops a new evolutionary sampling technique to balance microarray data, but the abstract does not say whether it creates synthetic examples or only selects instances.
The phishing detector reuses a standard CVAE for class-conditioned augmentation and feature extraction, and no change to the generation itself is described.
The spectrum sharing framework proposes propagation-aware undersampling and oversampling compared with existing schemes, but the abstract does not say whether synthetic examples are generated.

A GAN for general structured data generation, motivated by privacy and ML use, adds a multi-category generator for imbalance, so its purpose is broader than imbalanced classification (clarification 1).
The fault detection framework names an Enhanced Ensemble-SMOTE as part of its novelty without saying what is changed, so it cannot tell whether the oversampler is new.
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes LSD-SMOTE, interpolating in a disentangled beta-VAE latent space, but only claims enhanced performance without naming data or experiments.
Rebalances defect image classes with texture-synthesis images plus a quality filter in a study framed as an evaluation, and the abstract cannot tell whether the generator is new or applied.
No abstract, and a variational LSTM autoencoder for class-biased sarcasm detection may or may not generate minority examples.
The tunnel hazard text classifier introduces a SMOTE-based multi-strategy augmentation, but the abstract does not say whether it changes SMOTE or combines existing steps.
Proposes a Gaussian noise injection oversampler for the minority class as an alternative to SMOTE and ADASYN, evaluated with five classifiers on bank fraud data.
Existing RSMOTE combined with existing ENN cleaning is presented as a proposed COU model for software defect prediction, with no change to the generation described (clarification 3).
A SMOTE-enhanced estimator built for sufficient dimension reduction, a purpose other than imbalanced classification (clarification 1).
FusedRCE combines PCA, k-means plus SMOTE oversampling and Tomek link cleaning for insurance fraud, existing generation and cleaning steps presented as a new procedure (clarification 3).
tSMOTE generalizes SMOTE to impute missing observations in irregular time series before classification, a purpose other than class imbalance (clarification 1).
The intrusion detection pipeline uses an existing conditional GAN to balance samples before an LSTM classifier, and no change to the generator is described.
Proposes a new bagging-based oversampling that oversamples the minority class inside the bagging subsets of a credit-risk ensemble, evaluated on a bank dataset and five public datasets.
Introduces ClusIM, a new hybrid of k-means clustering and oversampling presented as its own method, evaluated with F-measure and G-mean on several datasets.
The flood prediction model adopts standard SMOTE as a separate data enhancement module, and its new part is an AdaBoost training strategy for a sparse Bayesian classifier.

FuzzyCSampling combines fuzzy c-means clustering with data sampling and is compared with undersampling and SMOTE variants, but the abstract does not say whether it generates synthetic minority examples or only undersamples.
The cross-project defect pipeline uses standard SMOTE and outlier removal before mRMR feature selection and a deep ensemble, presenting no new resampling.

The intrusion detection system's two-stage resampling combines existing SMOTE with existing NearMiss-1 undersampling and is presented as unique, with no change to the generation described (clarification 3).
The respiratory radar classifier implements a two-stage augmentation with DTW-based SMOTE-TS, and the abstract cannot tell whether this time-series SMOTE is the authors' own or an existing one.
Presents repeated SMOTE, applied once per minority class, as its scheme for balancing multiclass data, evaluated on the Glass dataset, though its novelty is doubtful.
I2 not stated in the abstract: proposes PSS-SMOTE, generating samples in a reconstructed phase space, supported only by theoretical analysis.

Mostly a study of Bayesian network classifiers on 129 imbalanced datasets that adds minority oversampling to a target imbalance ratio, and the abstract cannot tell whether that oversampling is synthetic or new.
No abstract, and the title names a boundary-focused, feature-aware oversampling for IoMT intrusion detection but also calls the paper a comparative study, so new versus applied is unclear.
